cells.tense: You are here with what hasn't been decided yet, and the not-knowing is part of the work.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've been carrying as only possible and set it on a real surface today. Say the next step out loud, then do only that step.
cells.core:
You are standing in the open part of your life, where little has been settled and you're in no rush to settle it. You can hold a thing that hasn't taken its shape without grabbing for one, and you can stay in a room while the answer is still out. That steadiness is the work — you carry weight without going stiff, and you stay available while you hold it.

This part is going well when it looks small and ordinary. You pick something up, give it a real place, and let it be what it is for now instead of pressing it into a shape it isn't ready for. You don't need to see how it turns out to take the next short step.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what has no shape yet without forcing it into one.
cells.verb: Holding what hasn't taken its shape yet and letting it settle without forcing the settling.
cells.place: A table where you set down what you're carrying and leave it there for a while.

cells.tense: You are braced for a version of your life that hasn't arrived, and the bracing wears down today.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been keeping open and put it in a real place today, messy and unfinished. Leave it there and don't rename it as still forming.
cells.core:
You're holding more possibility than one person can carry, and you keep every version alive by refusing to put any of them down. The bracing is for a future you can't write in from here. When something asks to be finished, you tell yourself it's still forming, still worth keeping, not yet the moment — and nothing gets room to grow.

The better version of this is plainer. You're steady and unhurried, and things take the shape they take around you because you're not gripping them. Today that means putting one of them down where it can be seen, unfinished and not explained away by another maybe.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding too many futures open and none of them can start.
cells.verb: Holding what hasn't taken its shape yet and letting it settle without forcing the settling.
cells.place: A table where you set down what you're carrying and leave it there for a while.

cells.tense: You are still standing as if the door were ahead, and the door is not ahead.
cells.ask: Find one small thing that isn't finished and make a single mark on it, even badly. No one has to see it. Do it again tomorrow if that helps.
cells.core:
You've been making your life from the narrow end, from the part that had to stay tight to keep things from getting worse. The easy reach toward what might be — you don't use it. You still carry what needs carrying. You just carry it alone and don't let anything new in past the grip.

The working version of this is modest. You make something without needing it to turn out well, and you do it before thinking it through. One mark on something unfinished today, badly if that's what it is. The reach comes back by being used, not by deciding to have it.

cells.verb: Holding what hasn't taken its shape yet and letting it settle without forcing the settling.

cells.tense: You are steering through the day from a practical crouch, and the road has more turns than you're taking.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've called necessary and say it out loud as something you chose — the route, the hour, the person you texted. Then name one other way you turned down.
cells.core:
Your hands are on the wheel, and you call the trip required. You hold steady, you carry what needs carrying, and you do it so automatically that it feels like the only road there is. The steadying is real. You're also the one choosing it, like it or not — you're not in a corridor with one exit.

Done well, this is just naming the turns. You look at a small decision from the last day and describe it as yours: the route you picked, the hour you set, the call you made. And you mention the other way you didn't take.
cells.sheetLine: You are steering while calling the trip required, and there are other turns.
cells.verb: Holding what hasn't taken its shape yet and letting it settle without forcing the settling.
cells.place: A table where you set down what you're carrying and leave it there for a while.
